title: Anthropic Launches Claude Meetings
content:
Anthropic announced new workplace features on Tuesday, including Claude Meetings, which brings Claude into video calls to begin working on tasks while participants are still talking. The company also unveiled Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets.
The launch of Anthropic’s new productivity-focused features comes just a few weeks after OpenAI unveiled a series of workplace tools that allow users to collaborate with ChatGPT to do things like visualize company information and create presentations, as both companies compete to turn their products into office suites of sorts to take on Microsoft and Google. Meta is also joining the competition with its Muse AI agent, which can build mini-apps on the fly to help users complete specific tasks.
With Claude Meetings, teams can add Claude to a video call as a visible participant. Claude then follows the conversation and gets to work on tasks in real time. As participants talk, it can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information, such as last year’s figures. After the call, the meeting notes, action items, and other materials Claude created are available in claude.ai.
The work that comes out of a meeting usually starts after everyone hangs up, but with this new feature, teams can turn discussions into actions in real time, Anthropic says.
Claude identifies itself as a meeting participant and posts a notice in the meeting chat. It won’t join calls with external guests unless authorized by an admin, and will automatically leave if an external guest joins.
Claude Meetings is launching in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. At launch, it works with Google Meet, with support for additional plans expected to follow.
As for Claude Whiteboards, Anthropic describes the feature as a collaborative board where teams can talk through a plan and have Claude turn it into an organized visual workspace with timelines and deadlines.
The company notes that many people already brainstorm with Claude, but that in order to share their results with others, they would have to copy-paste them somewhere else. Now, a team can work directly with Claude on the same board in real time.
When the brainstorm is done, Claude can turn the board into a doc or a slide deck. Additionally, Whiteboards also work inside Claude Meetings, so the board builds while people talk, Anthropic says.
Claude Whiteboards is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop, and mobile.
The company also launched Claude Sheets, which lets teams create and collaboratively edit spreadsheets with Claude. A team can ask it to build a campaign tracker or hiring budget, and Claude will then generate a working spreadsheet.
Anthropic says Claude handles the initial setup of trackers and budgets, while allowing teams to continue refining and updating the same spreadsheet. Each spreadsheet can include multiple tabs, formulas, formatting, and dropdown menus. Claude also makes edits directly in cells alongside the team, and outlines each change so users can see what it did.
Claude Sheets is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop and mobile.
Anthropic also announced that Claude Data, formerly known as Claude Dashboards, is now generally available. The feature connects Claude to systems that companies use to keep their numbers, like a data warehouse or CRM. Users can ask questions, and Claude responds with dashboards, written data stories, or narrated videos.
Additionally, the company announced interactive connectors that open the full version of apps like Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot inside Claude. Anthropic notes that teams can now open these apps directly alongside their Claude conversations and ask the assistant to work within them, essentially bringing existing workflows into the same workspace.

report.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Meetings, Whiteboards, and Sheets to turn live workplace discussions into real-time plans, tasks, and collaborative documents, intensifying its office-suite competition with OpenAI.
report.background: Anthropic’s launch reflects AI assistants moving from standalone chatbots into workplace suites. OpenAI recently unveiled ChatGPT workplace tools for visualizing company information and creating presentations, while Meta is testing Muse, an agent that builds mini-apps on demand. Microsoft and Google already bundle Copilot and Gemini into productivity software. To compete, Anthropic is adding native surfaces for meetings, whiteboards, and spreadsheets, where teams already create plans and decisions. Claude previously handled chat and app connectors but relied on copy-paste for shared artifacts. The beta rollout on Team, Enterprise, and paid plans—and Google Meet first—shows a cautious enterprise push with admin controls. Claude Data’s general availability and interactive connectors further position Claude as a workspace hub rather than just a model.
key_points: Claude Meetings joins Google Meet as a visible participant, follows conversation, and works in real time: drafting plans, mapping timelines on a whiteboard, answering chat questions, and pulling data from connected apps. After calls, notes, action items, and artifacts appear in claude.ai, aiming to turn discussion into execution before people hang up.

Anthropic added guardrails: Claude identifies itself and posts a chat notice, cannot join calls with external guests unless an admin authorizes it, and automatically leaves if an external guest joins. The feature is beta on Team and Enterprise plans, initially Google Meet only, with broader plan support expected later.

Claude Whiteboards provide a shared canvas where teams brainstorm with Claude and get organized timelines and deadlines; boards can become docs or slide decks and work inside Meetings. Claude Sheets generates collaborative spreadsheets with tabs, formulas, formatting, and dropdowns, and shows cell-level edits so teams can track changes.

Claude Data, formerly Claude Dashboards, is now generally available, connecting to data warehouses and CRMs to answer questions with dashboards, data stories, or narrated videos. Interactive connectors also open Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot inside Claude, bringing existing workflows into the same workspace.

The launch intensifies competition among AI labs to become office suites. OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft, and Google are all pushing agents into meetings, documents, and spreadsheets. Anthropic’s bet is that real-time collaboration—not post-meeting summaries—will differentiate Claude, though availability and enterprise trust will determine adoption.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the battleground is shifting from model quality to workflow ownership: meetings, docs, and spreadsheets are high-value entry points into enterprise software. Developers should expect more APIs and connectors, real-time agent architectures, and strict permission and audit requirements; integrations with Google Meet, Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot will matter as much as raw model capability. For regular users, Claude could reduce meeting admin and manual note-taking, but only if notices, guest controls, and data access are clear. Risks include vendor lock-in, inaccurate live artifacts, and privacy concerns. Adoption will hinge on reliability, admin controls, and whether teams trust an AI participant in sensitive discussions.
report.tools: Watch Claude Meetings beta (Team/Enterprise via Google Meet), Claude Whiteboards and Sheets on paid plans, plus Claude Data and interactive connectors. Compare OpenAI’s ChatGPT workplace tools and Meta Muse. For hands-on experimentation, explore Whisper-based meeting transcription and note-taking projects and real-time agent frameworks such as LangGraph or AutoGen; validate permissions, data retention, and external-guest handling before using them in sensitive meetings.
